chain.label: Wheel speed transducer harness design not error-tolerant
chain.trigger: Saab's design of the wheel speed transducer wire harnesses did not consider that the harnesses could be incorrectly installed during maintenance and overhaul

chain.label: Left MLG wheel speed transducer harnesses cross-wired during January 2017 overhaul
chain.trigger: the landing gear manufacturer's incorrect wiring of the wheel speed transducer harnesses on the left MLG during overhaul

caused_by.evidence: the bottom-end connectors...have no distinguishing feature to indicate which harness should be routed to the inboard wheel and which harness should be routed to the outboard wheel

chain.label: Undetected crossed antiskid wiring carried into revenue service
chain.trigger: This cross-wiring condition was not discovered until after the accident in part because the airplane was not in revenue service between the time of left MLG overhaul and PenAir's first revenue flight in June 2019. Also, the antiskid system does not generate a fault based on incorrect wiring.

caused_by.evidence: the harness that should have been routed to the left inboard wheel was instead routed to the left outboard wheel (and vice versa)

chain.label: FAA authorized Saab 2000 at DUT without assessing runway safety area dimensions
chain.trigger: the FAA's lack of consideration of the RSA dimensions at DUT during the authorization process that allowed the Saab 2000 to operate at the airport

chain.label: Captain qualified as PIC for DUT without required Saab 2000 experience
chain.trigger: he did not meet the total flight time in the Saab 2000 that the company's PIC airport qualification policy required...the captain might not have fully understood the challenges associated with landing the Saab 2000 at the airport

chain.label: Tailwind on runway 13 exceeding the 15-knot airplane limit
chain.trigger: the flight crew learned that the wind at midfield was from 300 degrees at 24 knots, indicating that a significant tailwind would be present during the landing

chain.label: Captain did not assert runway 31 preference; cursory crew discussion of runway choice
chain.trigger: the captain demonstrated poor CRM by not explicitly sharing his position about runway 31...the captain did not conduct the landing on runway 31 and instead yielded twice to the first officer's understanding, based on cursory discussions, that runway 13 should be used

chain.label: Crew continued landing on runway 13 despite known excessive tailwind (plan continuation bias)
chain.trigger: the flight crew's decision to land on a runway with a reported tailwind that exceeded the airplane manufacturer's limit was intentional, inappropriate, and indicative of plan continuation bias

caused_by.evidence: the flight crewmembers stated that they were aware of the airplane manufacturer's 15-knot tailwind limit but thought that the reported wind direction and speed (300 degrees at 24 knots) did not warrant a change of the runway for landing
With no definitive response from the captain, the first officer stated, about 10 seconds later, 'we'll try it again.' The captain then responded, 'last try.'
the captain's discounting of applicable items on the flight risk assessment form was consistent with a diminished recognition of the challenges associated with the flight

chain.label: Left MLG outboard tire entered a skid during landing rollout
chain.trigger: The initial evidence of the skid on the runway was a dark skid mark, consistent with the position of the left outboard tire, which began at 1739:57 (about 3 seconds after touchdown)

caused_by.evidence: when the airplane touched down on the runway, the tailwind was 15 knots...the groundspeed at MLG touchdown was about 142 knots

chain.label: Antiskid released inboard brake pressure and left the outboard skid unrelieved; tire burst, losing over 50% of wheel braking
chain.trigger: because of the crossed wiring, the antiskid system perceived that the left inboard wheel was skidding and released the brake pressure to that wheel and the right inboard wheel...the left outboard tire continued to skid and then burst, causing an additional loss of MLG wheel braking

caused_by.evidence: As a result of the incorrect (crossed) wiring, the antiskid system performance was substantially compromised
during most of the landing rollout, the left outboard tire was in a skid

chain.label: Airplane overran runway 13, the 300-ft RSA, and the blast pad
chain.trigger: the combined loss of left and right inboard and left outboard MLG wheel braking prevented the flight crew from stopping the airplane on the runway

caused_by.evidence: The airplane subsequently overran the end of the runway and the adjacent 300-ft runway safety area
Because an airplane requires more runway length to decelerate and stop when a tailwind is present during landing, a landing in the opposite direction (on runway 31) would have favored the wind

chain.label: Airplane struck perimeter fence, ditch, and road signs; propeller blades separated and entered cabin
chain.trigger: the airplane overran the end of the runway, passed through the airport perimeter fence, crossed a road, and pitched down over shoreline rocks with its nosewheel coming to rest at the edge of Dutch Harbor

caused_by.evidence: the airplane departed the end of runway 13 and traveled through the 300-ft runway safety area (RSA) and the 150-ft blast pad
the accident airplane would have been able to stop within an RSA that was suitable for the approach speed and size of the Saab 2000

chain.label: One passenger fatally injured, one seriously injured, eight minor injuries
chain.trigger: The passenger who received fatal injuries (seat 4A) was struck by a propeller blade that entered the cabin

caused_by.evidence: the left engine shed propeller blade fragments and two propeller blades...A left propeller blade impacted the left side of the cabin
